fixes.explanation: Samuel doesn't dance around it, friend. He says, “But today you have rejected your God, who saves you from all your troubles and afflictions…” (1 Samuel 10:19). Then he quotes what they told God: “No, set a king over us.” That's a heavy moment, and I think this one hurts.
That's him! After the tribe and the clan, “Finally, Saul son of Kish was selected.” (1 Samuel 10:21). It goes from the tribe of Benjamin, to the clan of Matri, to one man. One name, and it's his.

Ehud son of Gera was a Benjamite, so you were in the right neighborhood (Judges 3:15). But he isn't the man picked here. The text says “Finally, Saul son of Kish was selected.” (1 Samuel 10:21). Kish's boy is the one they're looking for.

Right on! They inquire of the LORD again, asking, “Has the man come here yet?” (1 Samuel 10:22). They ask the LORD, and He tells them where Saul is. That's a good habit for any baker when something goes missing.

Waiting around and hoping Saul turns up sounds reasonable, friend, but the text doesn't say that. What it says is “So again they inquired of the LORD…” (1 Samuel 10:22). They ask, “Has the man come here yet?” and the LORD replies.

Hidden! The LORD replies, “Behold, he has hidden himself among the baggage.” (1 Samuel 10:22). Think about that for a second. They looked for him and could not find him, and there he is, tucked in among the baggage. The text doesn't tell us why he hid, and I won't guess.

Resting among the baggage is a nice picture, friend, but that's not what the LORD says. His words are “…he has hidden himself among the baggage.” (1 Samuel 10:22). Back in verse 21, they looked for Saul and could not find him. The word here is hidden.

Samuel is the one doing the talking in this scene. The crowd's shout is about the man he's pointing to, Saul: “Long live the king!” (1 Samuel 10:24). Remember, the people asked for a king back in verse 19. Now they're cheering for one.

A scroll on a roof is a creative idea, friend, but the text says nothing like that. Samuel wrote the rights of kingship on a scroll and “…laid it up before the LORD.” (1 Samuel 10:25). That's where it goes.

That's it. The text says, “but Saul remained silent about it.” (1 Samuel 10:27). Those men despised him and brought no gifts, and he doesn't answer back. I can't say what Saul was feeling, but I think that took some restraint. If somebody sniffed at me in a meeting, I'd have a speech ready before the timer dinged.
That would make for a loud scene, friend, but it's not what happens. The text says “…Saul remained silent about it.” (1 Samuel 10:27). Silent is the word it gives.
